summary: The recorded base reproducibly drops out-of-range visual encoder layers through the broad PP layer regex. The exact candidate restricts PP filtering to normalized model.layers.N decoder names. Its regression and independent dense/MoE loader boundary and namespace cases pass, with no counterexample found within the original contract.

tests.what_was_measured: On base 358c163, Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration.load_weights with PP range [1,3) loaded decoder layers 1 and 2 but dropped model.visual.layers.3.weight and model.visual.layers.4.weight; the assertion requiring visual layer 3 failed.
At exact candidate bbaaba6, all 7 candidate tests passed, including the actual dense conditional-generation loader regression and helper namespace cases.

Both dense and MoE conditional-generation loaders excluded decoder layers outside [1,3), loaded decoder layers inside it, and retained visual layers 0, 3, and 5. Nine namespace/prefix boundary cases also matched the intended decoder-only classification.

gpu_execution.evidence: One gfx950 AMD Instinct MI350X was visible through PyTorch/ROCm, but the defect is deterministic Python name filtering before tensor device execution. No GPU numerical claim is made.

remaining_limitations: No Qwen3.5 checkpoint weights were available, so a complete checkpoint load and semantic model validation were not performed.
No multi-process, multi-node, or end-to-end pipeline-parallel serving workload was run.
The prepared host is AMD gfx950/ROCm 7.2 whereas the original report recorded NVIDIA H100/CUDA; the reviewed failure and fix are device-independent pre-device Python filtering.
The minimal fixtures qualify the actual load_weights filtering contract but do not qualify full-model serving or model accuracy.
